issues.concern: The headword '嫁' (yome) is often considered derogatory or old-fashioned when referring to one's own wife, making 'informal' an understatement. It can be offensive in modern usage.
The English translation 'My son's wife is coming next month' is too literal and misses the nuance of 嫁 in this context, which specifically means 'daughter-in-law'.
issues.suggestion: My daughter-in-law is coming next month.

issues.concern: The English translation 'The relationship between a wife and mother-in-law sometimes doesn't go well' is too general. '嫁' in this context specifically refers to the daughter-in-law in relation to the mother-in-law.
issues.suggestion: The relationship between a daughter-in-law and mother-in-law sometimes doesn't go well.
